stage: C3X 0.9.0-G10-P16 — Prospective Chess-Context-Conditional Intervention Router, Frozen Context→Grammar Assignment, Phase×Branching×Tactical Policy Partition, Grammar-Specific Structural/Preference Positivity, Global-vs-Routed Grammar Falsification, Held-Out Balanced Chess-Ecology Validation, Cross-Source Routing Stability, Frozen Defect-Replay Re-entry & Context-Adaptive Intervention Policy Experiment
scientific_conclusion: A structural-only chess-context router can be frozen without preference-outcome leakage and transfers to repo-unseen held-out TWIC arms.
The router improves preference-supported intervention yield directionally over GLOBAL_G2 on the identical held-out pair denominator: 9 vs 7 positions, with 3 ROUTED_ONLY and 1 G2_ONLY.
The improvement replicates in sign across both held-out sources (+1 position in TWIC 1655 and +1 in TWIC 1656).
However absolute routed positivity remains insufficient: 21.43% overall, 22.73% in TWIC 1655, and 20.0% in TWIC 1656, below the frozen 35% overall and 25% per-source gates.
The router's net gain is entirely produced by stricter G0 assignments in rich contexts; G1/G2 produce no net paired gain and G3 produces no positive held-out positions.
Therefore the missing object is not simply more context-specific grammar relaxation. Structural realizability is an insufficient routing criterion for preference-preserving intervention.

surviving_structure.positive: Context routing can improve held-out yield without relaxing the grammar globally.
surviving_structure.negative: Phase×branching×tactical structural coverage alone does not identify a router with sufficient preference preservation.
surviving_structure.strongest_signal: G0 tightening in selected RICH contexts creates all net routed-only gain.
surviving_structure.hardest_regime: REDUCED held-out positions have 0 positive interventions under both ROUTED and GLOBAL_G2 in this validation ecology.

forbidden_next_moves: Do not lower the 35% overall or 25% per-source positivity gates.
Do not open Stage C defect replay under P16.
Do not select router assignments using held-out preference outcomes.
Do not promote G0 globally from its local held-out gains.
Do not delete REDUCED or other hard contexts post hoc.
next_question: Which pre-outcome chess/search variables predict whether a structurally legal chain will preserve A/B preference support, and can those variables support a prospective intervention-admissibility classifier that generalizes across context/source without using edited-board outcomes?
